title: auth-api-401-429-debug-scratchpad-lena-2026-03-25
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad for the recurring 401 / 429 patterns we keep seeing from hosted-api. Use this to capture commands tried, timestamps, error blobs, and likely hypotheses.

Summary so far:
- Multiple customer reports (INC+Slack threads) referencing intermittent 401s and bursts of 429s around 08:00–09:30 UTC over past week.
- 401s tend to be short-lived (seconds->minutes) and often accompany a 403 for the same key shortly after.
- 429s appear when traffic spikes from a small subset of API keys; sometimes we see quota headers that don't line up with dashboard values.

Immediate repro attempts I ran (local):
1) Raw curl using API key header (simulates customer SDK without retries):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hey"}' \
     https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate | jq .
   Observed: occasional 401 responses. Verbose headers show:
   < HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
   < Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 08:12:07 GMT
   < Content-Type: application/json
   < Content-Length: 72
   body: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}

2) Replayed same request with same key 10x in quick succession (0.2s between requests) to check rate limit interaction:
   for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n"; sleep 0.2; done
   Observed sequence: 200,200,200,200,429,429,429,401,401,200
   Notes: 429s returned with header Retry-After: 3, but remaining header X-RateLimit-Remaining inconsistent (sometimes shows high remaining).

3) cURL with explicit X-Api-Key custom header (old SDK header):
   curl -H "X-Api-Key: sk_live_xxx" ...
   Observed same pattern. Suggests server not strictly tied to Authorization header parsing.

Server log snippets (from support dump):
- 2026-03-24T08:12:06Z request_id=req_Abc123 key=sk_live_xxx status=401 handler=auth error="signature mismatch"
- 2026-03-24T08:12:07Z request_id=req_Def456 key=sk_live_xxx status=429 handler=ratelimit error="burst limit exceeded"
- 2026-03-24T08:12:09Z request_id=req_Ghi789 key=sk_live_xxx status=200 handler=generate latency_ms=120

What I've ruled out so far:
- Key revoked: dashboard shows key active; account owner confirmed no manual revoke.
- Permanent expiration: keys are long-lived, no expiry on this tier.
- Client clock skew: I tested with servers + local set to NTP; Authorization is bearer token so no signed timestamps.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Backend auth cache inconsistency / race: auth service caches key state (active/disabled) in Redis with TTL. If rolling updates or cache invalidation hiccup occurs, some nodes may briefly believe key is invalid -> 401. That could coincide with rate limit state on other nodes -> 429.
2) Token reuse / token leak detection: we may have a detector that temporarily blocks keys if suspicious activity detected (pattern matching that flags high request rates from new IPs) and returns 401 vs 429.
3) Mixed routing to old auth microservice version: older version emits "invalid_api_key" for certain header formats -> 401. Newer version returns 429 with proper retry headers.
4) DB replication lag for account quotas: quota read from primary but sometime fallback to stale replica resulting in perceived high usage and 429s.

Evidence for (1):
- Timestamps in logs show back-to-back 401 and 429 for same key within 1–3s.
- Rolling deploy last night on auth-service (deploy-id: auth-2026-03-24-2) per release-engineering notes.

Quick checks to run next (actionable):
- Add a temporary debug flag that logs auth cache hit/miss and node-id in response headers for a small % of requests (internal only). Helps correlate which nodes are returning 401 vs 429. (Ping @Samir)
- Re-run a controlled burst test from two separate IPs/regions to see if IP-based heuristics are kicking in. Use scale test script on ci-agent-5 (low risk).
- Inspect Redis AUTH cache metrics (miss rate, failovers) around 08:00–09:30 UTC for last 7 days. (Ask infra/redis on-call for telemetry).
- Check deploy history for auth-service around 2026-03-24 and rollback timeline. (RE: auth-2026-03-24-2).

Quick commands to run (for others to copy):
- Repro single request with headers and print full response headers:
  curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -H "User-Agent: debug/1.0" -d '{"model":"redwood-1"}' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

- Burst test (simple):
  seq 1 20 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}:%{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -d '{"model":"redwood-1"}' https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate

Notes from customer reproductions (Slack snippets):
- "We get 401 for ~30s then everything is fine. Happened three times today at 08:14 UTC." - customer-a
- "We saw 429s with Retry-After 10 but our dashboards show we haven't hit quota" - customer-b

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we have per-node auth caches or a shared cache? (I think per-node with Redis backing; need confirmation)
- Does our fraud/abuse service ever return 401 to indicate temporary block? Confirm with security.
- Is there any recent change to header parsing (e.g., accept both X-Api-Key and Authorization)? Check PRs.
- Can we add more informative error codes for transient auth errors vs permanent? (UX request)

Possible short-term mitigations:
- For key owners: recommend exponential-backoff + jitter in SDKs; document typical Retry-After behavior for hosted API.
- Operational: temporarily increase observability (add node id + cache hit header) for a 1% sample to trap failing nodes.

Notes to self (next steps):
- 1) Ping Samir to add header logging flag and coordinate deploy to staging.
- 2) Ask infra to check Redis failover events for auth cache between 2026-03-17 and 2026-03-25.
- 3) Draft a short internal postmortem template if we confirm rolling-deploy correlation.

Scratch area (raw error blobs):
- {"error":{"type":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key invalid or expired"}}
- {"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Too many requests","retry_after":3}}

If anyone else is poking at this: leave notes below with timestamps and region/IP used so we can correlate with server logs.

-- Lena
